title: The Prestige
tagline: Two magicians, one trick, and no limit.
about: Two rival magicians in Victorian London go to any length to steal each other's greatest illusion.
cue: Serve the twin pies when Borden steps out on the far side of the stage.
faces: Matinee tea from 3. Doors close at curtain up.
The lights go down before the turn. Keep watching.
First the magician shows you something ordinary. White bread, mint butter, salted cucumber.
Birdcage devilled quail eggs with cress
Borden wrecks Angier's bird act. Quail eggs, mustard yolks, cayenne, cress.
Fallon's twin chicken and leek pies
Two men sharing one life. Matching pies, chicken, leek, tarragon cream.
Don't-forget-your-hat roast beef with Yorkshire puddings
Tesla tells Angier not to forget his hat. Rare roast sirloin, top hat puddings, gravy.
The prestige: Victoria sponge, sliced and restored
What vanished comes back. Butter sponge, raspberry jam, vanilla cream.
Tesla's machine crackles in Colorado. London dry gin, tonic, lime. Glows under black light.
A pot of English breakfast tea
Poured before the curtain goes up.
Prices include tea for one. Form TR-100. Images: TMDB

    The PledgeSomething ordinary: cucumber sandwichesFirst the magician shows you something ordinary. White bread, mint butter, salted cucumber.How to make it1 telegraph cucumber1 tsp sea salt flakes80g butter, softened2 tbsp finely chopped mint1 lemon8 slices of thin white bread1/4 tsp ground white pepperPeel the cucumber, slice it paper thin, toss with the salt and leave in a sieve for 10 minutes, then pat dry.Beat the butter with the mint and a little lemon zest.Butter every slice, lay the cucumber over half of them, add white pepper and close.Cut off the crusts and cut each sandwich into three neat fingers.Birdcage devilled quail eggs with cressBorden wrecks Angier's bird act. Quail eggs, mustard yolks, cayenne, cress.How to make it16 quail eggs2 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise1 tsp English mustard1/4 tsp cayenne pepper1 punnet mustard cressLower the quail eggs into boiling water for 2 and a half minutes, then plunge into iced water.Peel carefully, halve lengthways and tip the yolks into a bowl.Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard and a pinch of salt.Pipe back into the whites, dust with cayenne and top with cress.The TurnFallon's twin chicken and leek piesTwo men sharing one life. Matching pies, chicken, leek, tarragon cream.How to make it600g chicken thigh fillets, diced30g butter2 leeks, sliced2 tbsp plain flour300ml chicken stock150ml thickened cream1 tbsp Dijon mustard2 tbsp chopped tarragon2 sheets of frozen puff pastry, thawed1 egg, beatenBrown the chicken in the butter, then add the leeks and cook until soft.Stir in the flour, then the stock, cream and mustard, and simmer until thick; add the tarragon and cool a little.Divide between 2 identical small pie dishes, top each with pastry, crimp and brush with egg.Bake at 200°C until puffed and deep gold, then serve the two side by side.Don't-forget-your-hat roast beef with Yorkshire puddingsTesla tells Angier not to forget his hat. Rare roast sirloin, top hat puddings, gravy.How to make it1.2kg beef sirloin roast2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus extra for the tins1 tbsp hot English mustard140g plain flour4 eggs200ml milk1 tbsp plain flour, extra400ml beef stock1 tbsp horseradish creamWhisk the flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and rest it.Rub the beef with the oil, mustard, salt and pepper and roast at 220°C for 20 minutes, then at 180°C until rare in the middle.Rest the beef and turn the oven up to 230°C; heat a little oil in each hole of a deep muffin tin until smoking.Pour in the batter and bake, without opening the door, until tall like top hats.Stir the extra flour into the roasting tin juices, whisk in the stock and boil into gravy; serve the beef sliced with puddings, gravy and horseradish.The PrestigeThe prestige: Victoria sponge, sliced and restoredWhat vanished comes back. Butter sponge, raspberry jam, vanilla cream.How to make it200g butter, softened200g caster sugar4 eggs200g self-raising flour2 tbsp milk1 tsp vanilla extract150g raspberry jam250ml thickened cream1 tbsp icing sugarBeat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time.Fold in the flour, milk and half the vanilla and divide between 2 lined 20cm tins.Bake at 180°C until springy and golden, then cool on a rack.Whip the cream with the rest of the vanilla.Spread one sponge with jam and cream, put the other on top, dust with icing sugar, then cut it in front of everyone and put it back together.Pots and cupsTesla's glowing gin and tonicTesla's machine crackles in Colorado. London dry gin, tonic, lime. Glows under black light.How to make it160ml London dry gin800ml tonic water, chilled1 lime, cut in wedges2 cups iceFill 4 glasses with ice and pour 40ml gin into each.Top with tonic, add a squeeze of lime and stir once.Turn off the lights and shine a black light torch on the glasses: the tonic glows blue.A pot of English breakfast teaPoured before the curtain goes up.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
